title: Hybrid session-based IO smoothing experiment with enterprise SQ alignment
creator: Lina Patel
description: Investigate a hybrid per-session IO smoothing model that decouples immediate per-request token billing from invoiceable usage by applying a short session-level smoothing window and explicit grace credits for short-lived streaming conversations. This ticket scopes the experiment design, rollout, engineering tasks, and SQ (security questionnaire) talking points for enterprise contracts. Goal is to reduce billing-induced churn and enterprise disputes for interactive workloads while preserving unit economics and preventing abuse.
hypothesis: A brief session-level smoothing window (30-90s) with bounded grace credits will reduce invoice volatility for conversational apps and lower disputes without materially increasing per-token cost for sustained high-throughput customers. Combined with per-direction microtiers this will make billing more predictable for customers using streaming and short sessions.
success_metrics: Reduce streaming invoice variance (month-over-month) by >= 20% for pilot customers
Cut enterprise SQ billing disputes related to short sessions by >= 50% in pilot cohort
Billing accuracy >= 99.9% (no rounding or attribution errors) across 30-day pilot
No adverse change (>2%) in Redwood hosted API revenue from pilot cohorts
implementation_notes: Server-side: introduce session tokens (ephemeral) that group streaming connections for smoothing window evaluation
Metering change: store transient per-session ingress/egress counters and commit final billable delta at session close or after smoothing window expires
Edge cases: handle abandoned sessions (no explicit close) with TTL eviction and commit policy to avoid unbounded crediting
Quota/Rate limiting: ensure existing rate limiters integrate with session grouping to avoid bypass
Telemetry: emit per-session debug metrics (session_length, ingress_tokens, egress_tokens, smoothed_ingress, smoothed_egress, credit_applied) to billing pipeline
Billing pipeline: new converter to translate smoothed session deltas into invoiceable token lines with provenance metadata for enterprise SQ
Security: prepare SQ language describing token aggregation, no access to raw customer payloads during smoothing, and KMS/HSM usage for billing metadata keys
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dogfood for 2 weeks (console flag + feature gate) with engineering and Solutions Eng traffic
Phase 1: 3 enterprise pilot customers (opt-in) for 30 days; manual review of invoices and SQ artifacts
Phase 2: expand to 20% of PLG traffic with automated opt-in experimentation and A/B compare to control
Phase 3: full launch if success criteria met; update public pricing docs and SQ templates
Fallback: automatic revert to baseline billing if invoice divergence or abuse pattern detected
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end billing lines for smoothed sessions reconcile with raw token events (audit log) for sample windows
Console shows per-route/per-session cost breakdown and flags for smoothed sessions
SQ deliverable (one-pager + sample invoice) approved by Legal and Sales engineering
Telemetry dashboard for pilot metrics available and validated with synthetic traffic
Automated tests preventing double-counting or omission for session commit/TTL edge cases
tasks: Define exact smoothing window bounds (30s/60s/90s) and grace credit cap per session
Implement session token lifecycle in serving runtime and SDK handshake
Add per-session counters and export to billing pipeline
Instrument dashboard panels and alerting for invoice divergence
Draft SQ-friendly description and sample invoice lines for Sales/Legal review
Run internal dogfood and gather initial telemetry
